# Remepy secures $36m funding for hybrid drug pipeline expansion

The latest round brings the total capital raised by Remepy to $62m.

Salong Debbarma August 13, 2026

Share

 Copy Link
 Share on X
 Share on Linkedin
 Share on Facebook

  

Remepy develops hybrid drugs through partnerships with pharmaceutical companies. Credit: Gorodenkoff / Shutterstock.com.

Remepy has closed a $36m Series A financing round to accelerate its pharmaceutical co-development partnerships and expand its hybrid drug pipeline.

The proceeds will also be used to fund Remepy’s lead product Hybridopa’s global Phase III clinical trial targeting Parkinson’s disease (PD). It is set to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The latest funding brings the total capital raised by the company to $62m.

The Series A round was led by OG Venture Partners and M Ventures, Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany’s corporate strategic venture arm.

Other new and existing backers include NFX, Qumra Capital, Tadmor Group, TechAviv, and Vine Ventures. [...] Remepy develops Hybrid Drugs through partnerships with pharmaceutical companies.

These drugs combine prescription medicines with personalised, AI-driven therapeutic applications, aiming to integrate pharmacology with adaptive physical, cognitive, and behavioural interventions into a single treatment regimen.

The company stated that the Hybrid Drug model has gained traction, supported by evolving US regulatory frameworks for drug-software combination products.

Remepy recently disclosed a strategic partnership with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany to develop hybrid drugs for multiple indications, beginning with rare tumours.

Hybridopa, it’s lead programme for Parkinson’s disease, has reported positive Phase IIa clinical data regarding both motor and non-motor symptom improvement.

# Remepy Raises $36M Series A for Hybrid Drug Platform

Remepy raised $36M Series A led by O.G. Venture Partners and M Ventures for its Hybrid Drugs combining pharmaceuticals with AI digital protocols. The approach targets Parkinson's and oncology.

Emel Kavaloglu

Remepy (remepy.com), a New York-based company developing Hybrid Drugs that pair traditional pharmaceuticals with AI-driven digital protocols into a single regulated prescription, has raised $36 million in Series A funding led by O.G. Venture Partners and M Ventures. The approach combines the biological mechanism of a drug with personalized digital interventions measured and adapted by AI. The capital will advance Phase III trials of Hybridopa for Parkinson's disease and expand pharmaceutical partnerships. [...] ## Serial Founders Bring Biotech Credibility

Co-CEOs Dr. Michal Tsur, who previously co-founded Kenshoo (acquired by Skai), and Or Shoval lead the company. Scientific advisor Prof. Michal Schwartz from the Weizmann Institute brings pioneering neuroimmunology expertise.

## Phase III Trial and Pipeline Expansion Ahead

With deployments advancing, Remepy plans to initiate Hybridopa Phase III in Q4 2026 and pursue additional pharma partnerships in oncology and women's health.

Index [...] ## Strategic Investors Signal Pharma Validation

M Ventures, Merck KGaA's corporate venture arm, led the round alongside O.G. Venture Partners. The investment follows Remepy's April 2026 collaboration with Merck KGaA on rare tumors and other areas, validating the hybrid approach with a top-10 pharma partner.

## Digital Therapeutics Market Expands Rapidly

The digital therapeutics market is projected to grow from $10.9B–$12.6B in 2026 to $35.4B–$93.4B by 2031, with prescription DTx specifically moving from $5.6B in 2024 to $24.9B by 2032. Key drivers include the FDA's 2023 PDURS guidance and pharma's need for differentiation amid patent expirations.

Michal Tsur, Or Shoval and the team have built with such conviction, and today that looks like a $36M round co-led by M Ventures, the venture arm of Merck KGaA, the 350-year-old Darmstadt pharma giant with 60,000+ employees and over 20 billion euros in annual revenue, alongside our friends at OG Tech, bringing total funding to $62M with a phase 3 trial for Hybridopa in Parkinson's launching later this year.
Awesome to be in business here with our friends NFX, TechAviv, Naftali Bennett and others.
